_comment: Declared service topology for the week-01 synthetic platform.
This file is the AUTHORITY on which backend serves which endpoint, who owns
each, and which runbook applies. The app no longer rediscovers its own
architecture from whatever happens to appear in the selected window.
runbook_id scheme -- stable and readable, because these are the join keys to
the Week 2 corpus:  RB-<SERVICE CODE>-000  is the service-level runbook,
RB-<SERVICE CODE>-001 upwards are per-endpoint runbooks under that service.
The slo_* fields are DECLARED BUT NOT CONSUMED. Nothing computes an error
budget or a burn rate from them: six hours of data cannot support a credible
burn rate, and a number that looks like a burn rate but isn't is worse than
no number. They exist so a later week can use them, and so a reviewer can
see the thresholds were declared rather than reverse-engineered from the
same telemetry they are meant to judge.
No downstream external dependencies are declared (databases, third-party
gateways). Nothing in the telemetry can observe them, so declaring them
would be decoration -- an architecture diagram, not an operational fact.
